headline: AFC audit grades FAM finance 1.2 of 5; budget rarely reached a Congress vote since 2016
context: An AFC governance audit, shown only in part at FAM's 4 June 2026 congress, graded most of the body 'pre-intermediate' and found its annual budget rarely reached a Congress vote since 2016. FAM disputes a separate claim that it failed to table audited accounts.

cards.big: FAM cleared 94 governance reforms and called it a fresh start.
cards.sub: The AFC audit that forced them graded its finances 1.2 out of 5, and only part of the report ever reached the congress floor.

cards.big: FAM did not put its annual budget to a Congress vote for most years since 2016.
cards.sub: Honorary president Hamidin Mohd Amin said it may have been negligence. FAM says that for some of those years its own statutes did not require the vote.

cards.big: The audit graded FAM's finance function 1.2 out of 5, and rated most of the body 'pre-intermediate.'
cards.sub: This sits on a body steering tens of millions in public football money and still carrying a CHF 350,000 FIFA fine, about RM1.8 million, that arbitration refused to cut.

cards.big: Only part of the audit reached the congress floor; the AFC said the full report stays with FAM.
cards.sub: Bukit Gelugor MP Ramkarpal Singh says withholding it invites 'an adverse inference', and he will raise it in Parliament this month.

cards.big: Reform is the easy part. The harder question is who was watching while the budget members are meant to approve quietly went missing for years.
Picture a condo management that skips tabling its budget to owners for years, then passes a whole new constitution in a single meeting.
Public money is an amanah, and reform you cannot inspect is only a promise. The test is whether FAM will show the audit in full, not whether it can vote one through.

confidence: High on the spine. Budget-vs-accounts distinction, the 'only part presented' point, statute changes, and the CHF 350,000 fine + CAS dismissal are confirmed across three independent deep-research engines and, for the fine and the 2023 statute baseline, against PRIMARY records (FIFA Judicial Bodies releases, CAS media release, 2023 FAM Statutes). Audit scores (1.2 / 1.3 / 1.6, five-tier scale) rest on congress-presentation reporting because the AFC audit report itself is not public; this is disclosed in-copy via 'shown only in part'.
needs_verification: Card 3 'tens of millions in public football money' — confirm FAM is the steward of the cited allocations (RM30m development, RM65m NTC) rather than the money being channelled wholly via the ministry; soften to 'public football funding' generically if FAM stewardship of a specific sum cannot be cleanly stated.
Card 4 — confirm Parliament is sitting this month and that Ramkarpal's raise is still pending at publish date; if he has already raised or withdrawn it, update tense.
Card 4 — confirm the exact 'adverse inference' wording is Ramkarpal's (per A10) and attributed as his, not asserted by T4A.
Card 2 — confirm the 2020-2022 statute carve-out wording (FAM statement, A4) reads as 'no statute provision then', not as a blanket denial; the sub must not overstate FAM's defence.
source_notes: BUDGET vs ACCOUNTS (cardinal): AFC = budget not tabled for Congress APPROVAL since 2016; FAM denies the audited-ACCOUNTS claim (A3, A4) and says accounts were tabled every congress incl. FY2025. Cards say 'budget … to a Congress vote', never 'accounts'. SINCE 2016: softened to 'most years' — no engine verified a year-by-year primary sequence and FAM contests 2020-2022. FINE: CHF 350,000 ~ RM1.8m per CAS/Bernama (A12); CAS dismissed FAM's appeal, fine 'remains in place'; players' bans narrowed to official matches only (not used in cards). 'ONLY PART PRESENTED': corroborated beyond the MP by AFC sec-gen Windsor Paul John (per A6/NST); card 4 attributes the 'adverse inference' line to the MP and the 'full report stays with FAM' point to the AFC. SCORES: AFC report withheld; figures are congress-presentation reporting, disclosed in-copy.
